clues: The chief city of a state in southern Brazil sits on a high plateau. From there it rules the trade and the life of its state.
In summer, its high site and the rains of the season join to keep the heat down. Days stay warm here, but they rarely scorch.
In the eighteen hundreds, its spot between cattle lands and markets sparked a rich cattle trade. That trade drove the first big growth of the town.
In 2010, this city won a top world award for green town growth. The prize praised towns that build in a clean and lasting way.
A state university set up in 1912 stands as a proud old mark of this town. Its halls have taught crowds of youth for a century.
